name: Battle of Jena–Auerstedt
note: The plan shows the fight at Auerstedt only, around Hassenhausen. The accounts of Jena do not say how the two armies stood. The accounts give no compass directions, so the French are drawn at the foot and the Prussians at the head, with right and left taken from each side's own point of view. The hill behind which the French cavalry waited, and the exact spots of the Lissbach Stream and of the French and Prussian arrivals, are placed by judgement; the accounts do not say exactly where they lay. Oswald's infantry arrived with the Prince of Orange but is not drawn apart.

phases.title: Gudin deploys at Hassenhausen
phases.text: Gudin's Division was stopped outside Poppel by Prussian cavalry and artillery. Davout ordered it to deploy at Hassenhausen, while Schmettau's division and Blücher's cavalry formed to attack.
phases.quote: Once Davout became aware of the Prussian force, he ordered Gudin to deploy his force at Hassenhausen.

phases.title: Schmettau and Blücher push Gudin back
phases.text: Schmettau's troops and Blücher's cavalry attacked together. They pushed Gudin's troops back to the village of Hassenhausen.
phases.quote: Together, they attacked Gudin's troops and pushed them back to the village.

phases.title: Wartensleben arrives with the Duke of Brunswick
phases.text: Wartensleben arrived with the Duke of Brunswick, who ordered his infantry to the Prussian left flank and his cavalry to the right.
phases.quote: Wartensleben arrived at 8:30 a.m. with the Duke of Brunswick, who ordered his infantry to the left flank and his cavalry to the right.

phases.title: The French cavalry take their place
phases.text: The rest of the French cavalry arrived at 9 am and was placed on Gudin's left, where it waited behind the hill, out of the Prussians' sight.
phases.quote: The rest of the French cavalry arrived at 9 a.m. and was placed on Gudin's left.

phases.title: Friant's Division arrives on Gudin's right
phases.text: Friant's Division and the 12-pound artillery arrived at 9:30 am and moved up in squares on Gudin's right, so that the French line now reached out on both sides of the village.
phases.quote: General Louis Friant's Division and the 12-pound artillery arrived at 9:30 a.m. and moved in squares on Gudin's right.

phases.title: Friant's squares advance and Hassenhausen is attacked
phases.text: The advance of the French squares forced Blücher's cavalry back, and Blücher ordered his cavalry to attack. At that moment two of Wartensleben's regiments attacked Hassenhausen.
phases.quote: The advance of the French squares forced Blücher's cavalry back.

phases.title: The French cavalry strike from behind the hill
phases.text: Davout hid his chasseurs à cheval behind a hill and released them at a crucial moment, putting Blücher's cavalry to flight. Three Prussian cavalry regiments were routed and the infantry fell back.
phases.quote: hiding his chasseurs à cheval behind a hill and then unleashing at a crucial moment to put to flight Blücher's cavalry

phases.title: Brunswick orders a full assault on Hassenhausen
phases.text: With the cavalry routed and the infantry falling back, the Duke of Brunswick ordered a full assault on Hassenhausen. Schmettau's Division and Wartensleben's troops pressed on Gudin's line.
phases.quote: Shortly before 10 a.m., he ordered a full assault on Hassenhausen.

phases.title: Orange and Morand arrive
phases.text: With Brunswick and Schmettau wounded, the Prussian command had broken down. The Prince of Orange arrived and the King split his command between the flanks, while Morand's Division was sent to secure Gudin's left.
phases.quote: to split Orange's command in two, half to each flank. On the French side, Morand's Division arrived and was sent to secure Gudin's left.

phases.title: The French counter-attack
phases.text: Davout could see that the Prussians were wavering. He ordered his infantry to counter-attack, and Gudin's Division went forward against Schmettau's line.
phases.quote: Davout could now see that the Prussians were wavering and so at 11 a.m. he ordered his infantry to counter-attack.

phases.title: The Prussian centre breaks and the King orders a withdrawal
phases.text: Schmettau's centre was broken and forced back over the Lissbach Stream. Blücher's cavalry was blown, Wartensleben was trying to reposition his troops, and the King ordered a withdrawal.
phases.quote: By noon Schmettau's center was broken and forced back over the Lissbach Stream
